original_value: The secure transmission of data within a network has received great attention. As the core of the security management mechanism, the key management scheme design needs further research. In view of the safety and energy consumption problems in recent papers, we propose a key management scheme based on the pairing-free identity based digital signature (PF-IBS) algorithm for heterogeneous wireless sensor networks (HWSNs). Our scheme uses the PF-IBS algorithm to complete message authentication, which is safer and more energy efficient than some recent schemes. Moreover, we use the base station (BS) as the processing center for the huge data in the network, thereby saving network energy consumption and improving the network life cycle. Finally, we indirectly prevent the attacker from capturing relay nodes that upload data between clusters in the network (some cluster head nodes cannot communicate directly). Through performance evaluation, the scheme we proposed reasonably sacrifices part of the storage space in exchange for entire network security while saving energy consumption.

result.paraphrase: Secure data transmission in networks has attracted considerable attention. As the core of the security management mechanism, key management scheme design still requires further study. In response to the security and energy-consumption issues noted in recent papers, we propose a key management scheme for heterogeneous wireless sensor networks (HWSNs) based on the pairing-free identity-based digital signature (PF-IBS) algorithm. The scheme uses PF-IBS to perform message authentication, making it safer and more energy efficient than some recent approaches. In addition, the base station (BS) serves as the processing center for the network’s large data volume, which reduces energy consumption and extends network lifetime. Finally, it indirectly prevents attackers from capturing relay nodes that upload data between clusters in the network, since some cluster head nodes cannot communicate directly. Performance evaluation shows that our scheme reasonably trades some storage space for overall network security while saving energy.
